stem: A client with a mechanical mitral valve replacement is receiving warfarin. What target INR is recommended by the current ACC/AHA valvular-heart-disease guideline?
rationale: The ACC/AHA valvular-heart-disease guideline recommends vitamin K antagonist anticoagulation with a target INR of 3.0 for a mechanical mitral valve replacement. Other mechanical valve positions and selected valve types/risk profiles can have different INR targets, so the mitral position in the stem is essential. Therefore B is correct. The 2024 ACC/AHA valvular performance measures continue to reinforce appropriate VKA anticoagulation for mechanical prosthetic valves, with the 2020 guideline remaining the applicable ACC/AHA management guideline in 2026.
educational_objective: For a mechanical mitral valve replacement, recognize the ACC/AHA warfarin target INR of 3.0 and distinguish it from targets used for other prosthetic-valve situations.
source_organization: American College of Cardiology (ACC) / American Heart Association (AHA)
source_document_title: 2020 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Valvular Heart Disease — Key Perspectives, Part 3; 2024 ACC/AHA Valvular and Structural Heart Disease Performance Measures
source_version_date: 2020 guideline; 2024 performance measures; currentness live-rechecked August 16, 2026
source_locator: ACC Key Perspectives Part 3 > Prosthetic valves antithrombotic therapy: mechanical mitral valve replacement — INR of 3.0. 2024 ACC/AHA performance measures: VKA at an appropriate INR goal remains a performance measure for mechanical valve prostheses.
source_claim_supported: Mechanical mitral valve replacement requires VKA anticoagulation with a target INR of 3.0 under the applicable ACC/AHA valve guideline.

source_original.stem: A client with a mechanical mitral valve replacement is receiving warfarin. What target INR is recommended by the ACC/AHA valve guideline?
source_original.rationale: ACC/AHA guidance specifies a target INR of 3.0 for a mechanical mitral valve replacement. Option B is correct. Other mechanical valves may have different targets, which is why the stem specifies the mitral position. The other numeric targets do not match the guideline target for this valve position.
source_original.source_detail: Prosthetic-valve antithrombotic therapy: mechanical mitral valve replacement requires vitamin K antagonist anticoagulation with a target INR of 3.0; targets differ for mechanical aortic valves/risk profiles. 2020 ACC/AHA Valvular Heart Disease guideline remains the current ACC/AHA valve guideline in 2026; next major update is anticipated in 2027; currentness live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: medication administration, adverse effects/interactions, reversal, monitoring and teaching. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the numeric INR construct and key B after currentness verification. Added 2024 ACC/AHA performance-measure corroboration that mechanical prosthetic valves still require VKA at the appropriate guideline INR goal, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium because the final item is a direct guideline-target recall question.

audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item asks for the target INR, not the therapeutic range, and specifies the mechanical mitral position to avoid confusion with aortic prosthesis targets.

distractor_audit.A: Below the guideline target for mechanical mitral replacement.
distractor_audit.C: Not the target; 3.5 may appear as an upper end in some therapeutic-range descriptions but is not the ACC/AHA target value asked here.
distractor_audit.D: Above the guideline target and not recommended as the routine target.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only 3.0 is the guideline target for the specified mechanical mitral valve replacement.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are plausible numeric INR values and are formatted identically.
